Package App

Class App

java.lang.Object
javafx.application.Application
App.App
public class App extends javafx.application.Application
JavaFX application entry point and global screen router for the MIRAGE system.

This class extends Application and serves two distinct roles:

  1. Application bootstrap: The start(Stage) method is called by the JavaFX runtime after the platform is initialised. It configures the primary window (title, size, resize lock) and loads the first screen.
  2. Global screen router: showScreen(String) is the single method used by every screen controller to navigate between screens. It replaces the current scene entirely rather than pushing onto a navigation stack, which keeps state management simple for a desktop kiosk-style app.

Screen naming convention

Screen names passed to showScreen(String) must match the FXML filename under /ui/ exactly (without the .fxml extension), e.g. "GuestScreen", "ReservationScreen", "CheckoutScreen", "HotelSuiteScreen", "ConciergeScreen", "ReportScreen".

Stylesheet loading

The global stylesheet (/util/AppColors.css) is applied to every scene after loading, ensuring consistent theming across all screens regardless of what each FXML file declares inline.

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start(javafx.stage.Stage stage) throws Exception
      JavaFX lifecycle entry point. Called once by the JavaFX runtime after the application platform has been initialised.

      Responsibilities:

      • Stores the Stage reference for later use by showScreen(String).
      • Sets the window title, fixed dimensions, and disables resizing.
      • Loads the initial screen (GuestScreen) and shows the window.
      Specified by:
      start in class javafx.application.Application
      Parameters:
      stage - the primary Stage provided by the JavaFX runtime; never null
      Throws:
      Exception - if the initial FXML file cannot be loaded or the stylesheet cannot be resolved

    • showScreen

      public static void showScreen(String name) throws Exception
      Loads and displays the named screen by replacing the current scene on the primary stage.

      The method resolves the FXML file at /ui/<name>.fxml, loads it via FXMLLoader (which also instantiates and initialises the corresponding controller), wraps the result in a new Scene, applies the global stylesheet, and sets it on the primary stage.

      This is a full scene replacement — any state held by the previous controller is discarded. Controllers that need to preserve state should store it in a shared service or pass it through before navigating.

      Called by: every screen controller's navigation methods (e.g. goGuest(), goReservation(), etc.).

      Parameters:
      name - the screen name, matching the FXML filename without extension (e.g. "GuestScreen", "CheckoutScreen")
      Throws:
      Exception - if the FXML file is not found at the expected path, the controller class cannot be instantiated, or the stylesheet resource cannot be resolved
